title: Check reasoning with an external answer
goal: Compare answer-only and concise-explanation prompts against a known reference.
explanation: A request for hidden chain-of-thought does not guarantee accuracy and is not needed. Ask instead for a short calculation, stated assumptions and a checkable result. A polished explanation can rationalize a wrong answer. Use a puzzle with an external solution and keep the input identical across conditions.
sampleInput: Puzzle: A notebook and a pen cost $1.10 together. The notebook costs $1.00 more than the pen. What does the pen cost? Reference: pen $0.05; notebook $1.05; total $1.10 and difference $1.00.
prompt:
Solve the notebook-and-pen puzzle. State the answer, one short equation and a substitution check. Do not provide a private internal reasoning transcript. If you make an assumption, state it.
[Paste puzzle without the reference answer.]
workedExample: Let pen cost p. Then notebook costs p + 1.00, so 2p + 1.00 = 1.10 and p = 0.05. A $0.10 pen would imply a $1.10 notebook, totaling $1.20, so the tempting answer fails.

steps.title: Record the reference
steps.text: Hide the answer from the model and verify both total and difference yourself.

steps.title: Run answer-only
steps.text: Ask for just the price in a fresh hosted chat and save the unedited answer.

steps.title: Run a concise-check version
steps.text: Use the supplied prompt in a fresh context with the same puzzle.

steps.title: Evaluate both externally
steps.text: Substitute each answer into the original constraints; do not score by explanation length.

steps.title: Transfer the test
steps.text: Change the total to $1.30 with a $1.00 difference; the pen should be $0.15.

checks: Both responses are checked against the total and difference, not judged on fluency.
The report includes the $0.15 transfer case and its substitution check.
You do not claim that longer explanations prevent errors or reveal hidden internal reasoning.
commonMistakes: Rewarding a long explanation even when its arithmetic is wrong.
Leaking the reference answer into only one experimental condition.
offline: Solve the equation manually and compare the tempting wrong answer with the two original constraints.
reflection: Did the explanation improve the result, or only make it sound more convincing?

evidence.title: Keep the build
evidence.detail: Save your original input, exact prompt and resulting artifact. Both responses are checked against the total and difference, not judged on fluency.

evidence.title: Show what you tested
evidence.detail: Record a pass/fail result and evidence for every check below. The report includes the $0.15 transfer case and its substitution check.

evidence.title: Explain a limitation
evidence.detail: Write what changed after one deliberate revision and name a remaining failure mode. Rewarding a long explanation even when its arithmetic is wrong.
